review_notes: Read the whole file and searched Mathlib for existing equivalences between families of pairs and pairs of families. Found Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow, which has the same statement and the same toFun and invFun. The other declarations (piTensorHomEquiv and its simp lemmas) wrap piTensorHomMap and are legitimate named API. I did not check whether piTensorHomEquiv duplicates something else, such as an existing Mathlib equivalence for finite free modules. I could not compile the replacement, so the simp-set change in line 114 is untested. The unfolding of the private def in the simp set may need adjusting (for example using Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow_apply).

findings.excerpt: private def piProdEquiv : (∀ i, ν i × κ i) ≃ (∀ i, ν i) × (∀ i, κ i) where
findings.problem: This private def re-implements Mathlib's `Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow`. That equivalence has type `((i : α) → β i × γ i) ≃ ((i : α) → β i) × ((i : α) → γ i)`, with `toFun f = (fun c => (f c).1, fun c => (f c).2)` and `invFun p c = (p.1 c, p.2 c)`. These are the same type and the same maps as here, with the same dependent-family assumptions. The local copy adds nothing, and it forces the proof to unfold it by name in the simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `piProdEquiv`. Use `Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow ι ν κ` in `B.equiv C (Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow ι ν κ)` and in the final `.bijective` step. In the `simp only` call, replace `piProdEquiv, Equiv.coe_fn_mk` with the `@[simps]` lemmas of Mathlib's equivalence, `Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow_apply_fst` and `Equiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow_apply_snd`. These names are inferred from the `@[simps]` attribute and the replacement was not compiled.
findings.benefit: This removes a duplicate private definition and reuses Mathlib's standard equivalence together with its simp lemmas. Readers no longer have to check that a local equivalence equals the library one.

evidence.excerpt:
def arrowProdEquivProdArrow (α : Type*) (β γ : α → Type*) :
    ((i : α) → β i × γ i) ≃ ((i : α) → β i) × ((i : α) → γ i) where
  toFun := fun f => (fun c => (f c).1, fun c => (f c).2)
  invFun := fun p c => (p.1 c, p.2 c)

toFun p := (fun i => (p i).1, fun i => (p i).2)
  invFun q i := (q.1 i, q.2 i)
